review_notes: Read the whole file and the related WeightedExpose.lean, and checked Mathlib's Finset measurable-space API. The two Finset-valued measurability proofs (datumAccessibleLabels_measurable and datumBad_measurable) repeat the same non-trivial argument: preimage of a singleton, rewrite as an iInter via Finset.ext_iff, then a by_cases on membership with compl. The same pattern appears in WeightedExpose.recordedList_measurable. Mathlib already has `measurable_finset_iff`, so a repo-local helper is unnecessary. I have not compiled the proposed rewrites. The main uncertainty is whether the codomain `Finset (Fin N)` carries Mathlib's `Finset.instMeasurableSpace`; if the repo uses a different instance, a small local lemma would be needed instead. I did not report the other repeated bits (the unitTarget/targetStep norm bounds and the Kernel measurable lemmas) because they are short.

findings.problem: Both lemmas prove measurability of a Finset-valued map with the same hand-rolled argument. Each applies `measurable_to_countable'` and rewrites the fibre `{d | F d = f}` as `⋂ x, {d | (x ∈ F d) ↔ x ∈ f}` via `Finset.ext_iff` and `Finset.mem_filter`. Each then applies `MeasurableSet.iInter` and does `by_cases` on membership in `f`, using `hh` or `hh.compl` with `iff_true`/`iff_false` simp lemmas. The same pattern occurs again in WeightedExpose.recordedList_measurable. This reduces to a single fact: a Finset-valued map is measurable iff each `fun d ↦ x ∈ F d` is measurable. Mathlib already states this as `measurable_finset_iff`, so the ~20-line fibre/iInter/by_cases scaffolding is duplicated and unnecessary.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the scaffolding in both proofs with `rw [measurable_finset_iff]; intro x`. Then reduce the goal to measurability of a Prop-valued predicate with `measurableSet_setOf.1`. For `datumAccessibleLabels_measurable`, after `intro i` and `simp only [datumAccessibleLabels, Finset.mem_filter]`, the goal is `Measurable fun d ↦ i ∈ datumSelected g d ∧ datumHome hL d i = v ∧ datumAccessible hL g m t r R C S u i d`. Close it with `measurableSet_setOf.1 hh`, reusing the existing `hs` and `hh` sets, i.e. `hs.inter ((measurableSet_eq_fun ...).inter (datumAccessible_measurable ...))`. For `datumBad_measurable`, after `intro v` and `simp only [datumBad, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]`, close the goal with `measurableSet_setOf.1` applied to the existing `hh` preimage of `{s | 2*s.card<M}`. The `iff_true`/`iff_false` case split and the `Finset.ext_iff` fibre rewriting disappear. The same one-line reduction can serve `recordedList_measurable` in WeightedExpose.lean.
findings.benefit: Removes about 30 lines of repeated, fragile simp-and-case-split code. Each proof then states only its mathematical content: why the membership predicate is measurable. It also reuses a maintained Mathlib lemma instead of three slightly different copies of the fibre argument, so changes to the unfolded definitions (`Finset.filter`, `Set.ofPred`) have less to break.

evidence.excerpt: lemma measurable_finset_iff : Measurable g ↔ ∀ a, Measurable (a ∈ g ·)

by_cases hi : i∈a
  · simpa only [hi,true_iff] using hm
  · simpa only [hi,false_iff,←Set.compl_ofPred] using hm.compl
